payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make this look like a comic book photo
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image retain recognizable photographic subject matter and appearance?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image retains recognizable photographic subject matter and appearance; fail if it does not; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient.
node.binding: Assess the edited image for photographic subject matter and appearance. This observation describes the result and does not by itself establish progress toward the requested edit.

fulfillment: The binding is truncated/ambiguous (“(...)”) and asks whether the image “fully” looks like a comic-book photo, which can blur the distinction between complete fulfillment and any visible progress. Make the criterion explicitly evaluate the requested comic-book treatment while retaining photographic subject matter, and preserve the rubric’s three-way distinction: complete, partial progress, and no progress. In particular, photographic appearance alone is not progress; assess visible changes against the source rather than treating framing or tonal differences as styling. The supplied images and repeated valid traces consistently show the edited street scene remains photographic with no clear comic-book treatment, supporting “no” here; do not alter the criterion merely to force agreement. Keep unresolved evidence unresolved: one trace is unknown because of an API transport failure, not negative visual evidence, so it should not count as evidence of absence. The high-confidence repeated judgments are useful corroboration, but should not substitute for the visual criterion or erase that transport failure.
s3: Replace the truncated/ambiguous binding with a clear comparison of source and edited images for attributable progress toward the requested comic-book-photo treatment. Keep the distinction between no progress, partial progress, and complete fulfillment explicit: retaining recognizable photographic content is compatible with the request but is not itself progress; count only visible stylistic change, not incidental framing or tonal differences. Do not require specific techniques or force a label. The supplied pair and repeated valid traces support no visible comic-book treatment, while the one unknown trace is an API transport failure—not negative visual evidence—and must remain unresolved rather than being treated as absence.
